page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m2.xlarge is a virtual machine built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. Compute capacity is delivered by dedicated AMD EPYC processor cores operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz across 4 vCPUs. The hardware configuration pairs these processing resources with 8.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Discrete graphics acceleration is not included, maintaining a purely CPU-driven computational profile.

The instance contains no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached block volumes to handle operating system installations and persistent workloads. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth limit of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance provides a higher core count relative to memory size compared to standard 1:4 general-purpose tiers, presenting a structural tradeoff suited to compute-centric routines that do not experience high per-thread memory pressure.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource ratio allows deployments to leverage dedicated AMD EPYC cores without paying for unneeded memory capacity. This configuration makes the ecs.u2a-c1m2.xlarge instance suitable for stateless application hosting, containerized web services, continuous integration build nodes, API gateways, and distributed task workers that execute moderate computational jobs within an 8 GB memory footprint.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m2.xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine deployed on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.25 GHz, it supplies 4 dedicated vCPUs alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per core. The instance provides no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage for non-volatile data persistence, and features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. Operating without discrete GPU hardware, it targets non-accelerated computing environments. The configuration emphasizes execution efficiency for multi-threaded processes that prioritize CPU execution density over expansive memory footprints. This architectural profile fits application tasks such as distributed web serving, lightweight microservices, front-end application hosting, background task processing, and automated build pipelines where a lean memory profile matches processing requirements.
